lens: CRO (Baymard/CXL school, D2C jewellery India): add-to-cart and checkout rate for a shopper landing from an Instagram ad at 360x640 in the in-app browser. Covers the first-screen decision set, the buy path (Add to bag, Buy now, sticky bar, the moment after adding), the 20% add-to-checkout drop, the Buy 2/3/4 ladder and AOV, COD vs prepaid, ad message match, friction/distraction, and the test plan.
renders_used: Fresh renders made from proto/prototype.html as it stands (the pdp10 renders are 12 s older than the HTML, so G3 applied): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aaed4e78-f5ea-57f6-bb8a-ea8f2c0ecee0/scratchpad/cro_r1/ (fold.png, added_300.png, added_twice.png, set_2added.png, fold-ad.png, slice_0..5.png, probe.json). Layout is identical to pdp10/fold.png; only the trust-row and fold wording differ.

criteria.note: All six decision items are on screen 1: worn hero 77-406, H1 418-447, price + incl. GST 454-484, ladder ₹2,159/₹1,919/₹1,679 495-548, ship line 555-573, bar 575 (probe.json). But the line reads 'Free insured delivery by 18–20 Nov' (HTML L189): 'by' with no 'est.' is the rubric's 6/10 courier-promise case. Slack above the bar is 2px, so a 620px-tall IG viewport puts COD under the bar. Ladder caption 9.5px and rung labels 10px gold (L60, L63) are barely legible.

The worn hero is right and nothing pops up. The bar is 97% opaque (L71) and Buy now has no fill, so the trust-row glyphs ('Waterproof,', 'Faulty? Sorted', 'Arrives in the') and the gift-box icon ghost through both buttons (cro_r1/fold.png y 1240-1280 at 2x). The 'VIDEO' chip (L177) is a <span> that does nothing: a dead tap on the first screen, on a route that already carries 96% of the site's rage clicks.

Gate G1 trips: Questions says 'does not tarnish or turn your skin' (L262), which caps the page at 60 whatever the CRO work does. Outside-FACTS claims: 'in a vacuum' and 'far harder than regular plating' (L214), 'store it flat in its pouch' (L257). 'Faulty? Sorted within 7 days' (L194) presents the 7-day reporting window as a resolution time. 'in her own video' (L221) undercuts the paid/barter creator disclosure.

Real photos, the gift box, a WhatsApp contact and '@riya · creator' on reel 1 are all present. Against that: five grey ★ in the empty state (L231, the 6/10 anchor), reel 2 has no creator label, @naira.flore never appears, the reel play buttons are dead <span>s, and nothing proof-like sits on the first screen except the photo.

The fold text matches the policy (L252). But the trust row misstates it and sits under the bar on screen 1, the fold header says 'returns', there is no link to /exchange-return-policy, and the first-screen date has no estimate wording.

The ladder shows once, on screen 1, in correct per-piece rupees, with no NAIRA10 and no second offer (the ticker is gone, which is good). The gap: the line carrying 'automatic, no code' is the smallest text on the page (9.5px gold, 3.7:1), and 'Any pieces' is vague.

The rail sits in the right place, uses real live pieces with correct maths (₹3,758 / save ₹939) and a true 'Only 3 left'. It is broken as a buy path, though. (1) '+ Add' never touches the bag, yet the card shows '✓ ADDED' and the panel says '3 pieces in your bag ₹3,758' while the bag badge is empty (cro_r1/set_2added.png). (2) Tapping Add to bag, picking 2 pieces, then 'Add the set' leaves the bag at 4 with TWO bracelets: the toast says '30% off applied' while the panel says 20% (seq.js). (3) The third card is the Cushion Halo Ring, the only rhodium match and the piece Riya wears with the bracelet in reel 2, and it is cut at x=300 with its name truncated. (4) The Add buttons are 36px (measure.json smallTapTargets).

'COD available' is on the first-screen line in the owner's wording, and no prepaid discount is stated. But Buy now lost the UPI marks the owner asked for on buy buttons (live JDN L1173/L1380 UpiBadges). The fold's 'any COD fee is shown in your bag before you pay' (L252) is false on the Buy now path, which skips the bag. The PROPOSED prepaid line has no notes block in the prototype.

Scored for the buy-path targets and legibility only. Primary buttons are 48px. '+ Add' is 36px, 'Ask us on WhatsApp' 40px and the hero heart 40px. The WhatsApp link renders in default blue with an underline (cro_r1/slice_3.png). Ladder labels are 10px gold at 3.7:1. The page uses lang='en', not en-IN.

The bar was visible at every 200px scroll step (probe.json scroll), carries the price and never covers the facts. Against it: Buy now is a <button> with no handler, the 'Added · view bag' state re-adds the piece instead of opening the bag, the bag icon has no handler, and the bar does not step aside at the footer.

18 image requests (651 KB) load before any scroll, with no loading=lazy, no fetchpriority, no width/height and no srcset (grep). Google Fonts loads 7 faces (Cormorant 400/500/600/400i, Jost 300/400/500), and 600 and the italic are unused. A file:// LCP of 492 ms says nothing about the network, so this is scored on design intent per the rubric.
cmp cro_r1/fold.png cro_r1/fold-ad.png: IDENTICAL. The HTML has no URLSearchParams or utm handling. Nothing echoes the ad.

The button changes state and the badge updates. The toast (L145, bottom:76px) sits over the ladder prices and the delivery line (added_300.png y 1042-1128 at 2x), is gone after 2.6 s (L317), has no checkout or bag action and no aria-live, and states progress as '10% off' rather than rupees. Re-tapping 'Added · view bag' adds a second ₹2,399 bracelet (bag 2, toast 'Add 1 more · 20% off', added_twice.png): accidental quantity, in the family of the basket sneaking CCPA lists [S29].

There is no bag render, and Buy now has no target to verify. The rail announces a bag total (₹3,758) that is not in the bag, and the add-set path quietly puts a second bracelet in the bag to reach 30%. The bar keeps saying ₹2,399 after pieces are added. Price certainty breaks before the shopper ever reaches the bag.

fixes.change: Rebuild the moment after Add to bag. (a) Add to bag adds exactly one unit. Once the bracelet is in the bag the button never adds again; quantity changes only in the bag. (b) The sticky bar switches to [CHECKOUT · ₹2,399] (ink, 1fr; the bag total after the ladder; goes straight to Fastrr with the bag and its one ladder code; fires InitiateCheckout) + [BAG · 1] (outline, 128px; opens the drawer). (c) Delete the toast. In its place a non-modal card lies over the LOWER gallery only (16px side margins, top 230, bottom 398, ivory, 1px var(--line) border, radius 0, role=status aria-live=polite). It has no timer and closes on its 44px ×, on 'Keep browsing', or after 150px of scroll. Copy, in order: 'Added to your bag · Prism Rivière Bracelet'; 'Any second piece takes 10% off your whole bag.'; a row with a 56px Cushion Halo Ring thumb, 'Cushion Halo Ring · adds ₹659, not ₹999' and an 88x44 '+ ADD' button; then the bag's own line 'COD fee ₹120 · none if paid online' (5% of ₹2,399, recomputed live; owner to OK it here). The price, the ladder and the delivery line stay uncovered, and the checkout control stays in the thumb zone. Figures come from promo.ts addOnEffect/pdpOfferStatus, which already produce 'adds ₹659, not ₹999'.
fixes.why: C20, C21. ATC→IC is 20.1% (28d), the lowest step on the funnel and flat across all six top ads, which points at the site rather than the creative [N research_data §4-5]. Today the toast covers the ladder prices and the ship line (added_300.png), lasts 2.6 s and offers no checkout. A second tap on 'Added · view bag' adds a second bracelet (added_twice.png: bag 2). NN/g: clear add feedback with 'continue shopping' [S13]. Putting Checkout where the thumb already is cuts Add → drawer → Secure Checkout to Add → Checkout. Showing the COD fee before Fastrr removes drip-pricing doubt [S29].

fixes.change: Make the rail's state true and idempotent. '+ Add' really adds that piece to the bag: the badge updates and the button reads '✓ IN BAG', which removes the piece on a second tap. The summary reads from the bag, never from card selection: 'Your bag · 2 pieces · ₹3,058 / 10% off applied · you save ₹340 / A third piece makes it 20%'. 'Add the set' adds only pieces not already in the bag and the bracelet at most once. Its label follows state: empty bag 'ADD ALL FOUR · ₹3,987'; bracelet already in 'ADD THE OTHER THREE · BAG ₹3,987'; with a line above it '30% off everything · you save ₹1,709'. The sticky bar's price follows the bag total.
fixes.why: C7, C21, C3. Probe (cro_r1/seq.js): picking hoops and necklace shows '✓ ADDED' and '3 pieces in your bag ₹3,758' while the bag is empty. Add to bag → pick 2 → Add the set gives bag = 4 with two bracelets, a toast saying '30% off applied' and a panel saying 20%. A shopper who believes the set is in the bag and taps Buy now pays for one piece, or gets an unwanted second ₹2,399 bracelet: basket sneaking under CCPA's dark-patterns list [S29]. Maths: ₹5,696 × 0.7 = ₹3,987.2 → ₹3,987, rounded once as promo.ts discountedSubtotal does.

fixes.where: Questions (L262), Up close row 2 (L214), Care (L257), trust row (L194), fold summary (L251), Worn by (L221, L224), reviews (L231)
fixes.change:
Clear gate G1 on and around the buy path. Questions: 'No. It is surgical stainless steel with a PVD rhodium coating: waterproof and tarnish free.' Up close row 2 body: 'PVD rhodium coating on surgical stainless steel. Waterproof and tarnish free, so daily wear and water are fine. Keep it away from perfume and harsh chemicals.' Care: delete 'and store it flat in its pouch'. Trust row: 'Faulty piece?
Tell us within 7 days'. Fold summary: 'Delivery, COD & faulty pieces'. Worn by sub: 'Riya, a creator we work with, styling it with mehendi.' Reel 2 label: '@riya · creator · with the Halo ring'. Delete the ★★★★★ div.
fixes.why: C3 (G1 caps the whole page at 60, so no CRO gain survives it), C4, C5. 'turn your skin' is a Never-list skin claim; 'in a vacuum' and 'far harder' sit outside FACTS (rubric §5). 'Sorted within 7 days' promises a resolution time the policy never gives: 7 days is the reporting window. Unlabelled paid/barter creator content is CCPA 'disguised advertisement' [S29]. Grey stars read as a rating at a glance (C4 6/10 anchor).

fixes.change: (a) The delivery line reads exactly: 'Free insured delivery, est. 18–20 Nov · COD available'. Measured at 360px, it ends at x=333 of 344, one line. (b) The bar background is solid var(--ivory), not rgba .97, and .btn.now gets background:var(--ivory), so nothing ghosts through. (c) The hero height absorbs viewport variation instead of the facts: .track { aspect-ratio:auto; height:clamp(260px, calc(100svh - 311px), 440px) } (77 header + 167 facts + 2 slack + 65 bar). That keeps 329px at 640, shrinks on the ~600-620px IG Android viewports so COD never slides under the bar, and grows on taller phones.
fixes.why: C1 (the 'by' wording is the rubric's 6/10 anchor; FACTS: the window is an estimate, not a courier promise), C2 (glyphs and the gift-box icon ghost under both buttons in cro_r1/fold.png), C5. The facts end at 573 against a bar top of 575: 2px of slack is a coin-flip across real IG in-app viewports, and the COD line is the first casualty. Baymard: 64% look for shipping cost on the PDP before adding [S2].

fixes.change: Wire Buy now as the live one is wired: buyNow(this piece) → Fastrr directly, firing AddToCart then InitiateCheckout with the shared event_id scheme, so the pixel funnel stays comparable. Label: 'BUY NOW' plus the live UpiBadges (GPay/PhonePe/Paytm discs, size 15). Widen the column to 128px (grid-template-columns: 1fr 128px); 'ADD TO BAG · ₹2,399' still fits at 200px. When the bag holds at least one piece, this slot becomes the BAG/CHECKOUT state from fix 1, so Buy now can never silently check out one piece and drop a set the shopper built. Fold copy: 'any COD fee is shown before you pay', not '…in your bag…', which is false on the Buy now path.
fixes.why: C8 (10-today requires the payment marks; the owner asked for them on buy buttons), C21, C15. Today Buy now is a <button> with no handler (probe.json buyNow). 68-74% of orders are one piece, so Buy now IS the main path to an order. Android adds more than iPhone (14.8% vs 12.3%) but finishes checkout far less (16.6% vs 27.9% purchase/IC), and UPI is the Android shopper's default. Live code comment: Buy now 'checks out this piece on its own, without the bag's offer'.

fixes.change: Replace the 132px carousel with a 3-row vertical list, all visible at once, ordered by fit. Row: 72x90 thumb, full name in 16px serif, price + 11px strike, one 12px line of truth, the marginal-cost line in deep sage, and an 88x44 '+ ADD' button on the right. 1) Cushion Halo Ring, ₹999 (₹1,669 struck), 'PVD rhodium, like the bracelet · adjustable US 5–9', 'With the bracelet it adds ₹659'. 2) Prism Pear Drop Necklace, ₹999 (₹1,110), 'PVD 18K gold coating · Only 3 left', 'adds ₹659'. 3) Prism Emerald-Cut Hoops, ₹1,299 (₹1,629), 'Gold tone', 'adds ₹929'. Keep the heading 'Make it a set' and the sub 'Any second piece takes 10% off your whole bag, a third 20%, a fourth 30%.'
fixes.why: C7, C6. The ring, the best metal match and the pairing Riya actually wears, is the card hidden off-screen with a truncated name (cro_r1/slice_1.png). Baymard: 55% of sites truncate cross-sell titles and users ignore suggestions that lack detail [S10]. The marginal-cost framing ('adds ₹659, not ₹999') is already the live PDP's offer-line logic. AOV ₹1,511 against ₹979 ad cost per order makes the second piece the margin lever, and shoppers who buy two use the ladder (33 of 38 BUY2) [N].

fixes.change: Build message match at zero first-screen height cost. A tiny inline script before first paint reads utm_content, splits it on '_' and looks the tokens up in a map: { riya: { slide: 5, chip: '▶ From Riya's reel · creator' }, studio: { slide: 1 }, default: { slide: 0, chip: '▶ Riya's video · creator' } }. It sets track.scrollLeft before paint (no animation) and the chip text. The chip becomes a 44px-tall <button> that scrolls to Riya's slide and swaps the poster for the video on tap; no MP4 bytes load before the tap. Keep the query string, add no redirect, fall back to the default for unknown tokens. Ask the ads owner which real frame 'sugar' shows so prism_sugar_p1 gets its own entry.
fixes.why: C17: cmp fold.png fold-ad.png is identical and the HTML has no URLSearchParams. Meta: carry 'the same imagery and messaging from the ad' [S23]; Unbounce's one-verb match lifted conversion 31.4% [S25]. Today the 'VIDEO' chip is a dead <span> on the first screen of the route with 96% of the site's rage clicks.

fixes.change: g1: fetchpriority='high', width=720 height=658, never lazy. Every other image: loading='lazy' decoding='async' with width/height. That includes gallery slides 2-8, which Chromium lazy-loads inside the horizontal scroller. Use a srcset of 360w/720w/1080w from the Shopify CDN (&width=) with sizes='100vw' for the gallery and '72px' for rail thumbs. Fonts: request only Cormorant Garamond 500 and Jost 400/500 (600 and the italic are unused; draw the Jost 300 '+' at 400). Budget before the first scroll: at most 6 image requests and 500 KB.
fixes.why: C16. Probe: 18 image requests and 651 KB before any scroll, versus a budget of 6 and 500 KB. Vodafone: 31% better LCP gave 8% more sales in a 50/50 paid-traffic A/B [S18]. Facebook weighs site speed in ad delivery [S24]. The live page's eager loading (37 of 38) is one of the faults being replaced.

fixes.change: Ladder caption: 'Any pieces · no code needed', 11px, .14em tracking, deep sage #50726A (4.8:1). Rung labels 'BUY 2 · 10%': 11px, weight 500, deep sage. Rupees: 14px ink. 'each': 12px var(--ink-2). Price row: add a right-aligned 'Arrives gift-boxed' (12px, ink-2) in the 165px of free space after 'incl. GST'. This is true (it ships in the Naira Petite gift box), costs no height, and brings the trust row's gift point above the bar. Rerun fix 4c's clamp with the new facts height (+3px → calc(100svh - 314px)).
fixes.why: C6, C14, C1. The line that says the offer is automatic is the smallest, lowest-contrast text on the page (9.5px gold, 3.7:1), yet 'no code' is the ladder's whole advantage over coupon-wall competitors (GIVA, Palmonas, Salty) [N bench]. Baymard: 78% of sites show no gifting on the PDP [S1]. Today the gift box is visible only under the bar.

keep: The first-screen stack and its order: worn hero, H1, price with incl. GST and a small unbadged strike, the 3-rung ladder in this piece's rupees (₹2,159/₹1,919/₹1,679), one delivery + COD line, then the sticky bar. Everything is above the bar at 360x640 (facts 573 vs bar 575).
'ADD TO BAG · ₹2,399' as the single ink primary with the price on the button, and Buy now as the outlined secondary.
The sticky bar from first paint, never covering the facts, reachable at every scroll position (probe: visible at all 200px steps).
One offer only: no announcement ticker, no NAIRA10, no stacked codes, no % OFF badge, no FOMO, timers, sold counts or fake rating.
'Make it a set' directly under the trust row with live pairing pieces, real images, true 'Only 3 left' on the necklace, and ladder maths that match the bag's rounding (₹3,758 / ₹939).
The sub-line 'Any second piece takes 10% off your whole bag, a third 20%, a fourth 30%' is the clearest statement of the ladder on the page.
Details open by default with the spec in FACTS wording (18 cm, 15–19 cm, ~5 mm cushion CZ, fold-over clasp, surgical stainless steel with PVD rhodium coating).
The honest review empty state text ('We ask every customer… every review appears here as written') and the WhatsApp contact.
A short page (3,239px, about 5 screens) with a calm rhythm, Jost and Cormorant only, and no console errors.
The 'Worn by' section with Riya's mehendi styling: culturally on-target creator proof for the season, once it is labelled.
roadmap: Reviews (C4, the largest score_with_inputs gap): install Judge.me or Shopify Product Reviews, request reviews 7 days after delivery with photos, and show average + count beside the H1 only once this piece has 5 or more real reviews. Spiegel: 5 reviews give +270% purchase likelihood, more for higher-priced items [S16].

Prepaid nudge (C8): owner confirms the 5% PrepaidDiscount as a standing Fastrr offer (55 of ~105 prepaid orders already carried it). Then the after-add card and Buy now carry 'Pay online: ₹2,279' (5% off ₹2,399), and COD keeps equal weight. Expected value: COD is 44.7% of orders with 21.4% RTO against ~1% prepaid, so each 10pp shift to prepaid saves about 2% of orders from RTO, worth about ₹979 of ad cost each plus two-way shipping.
After-add COD line (C21): owner approves showing the bag's 'COD fee ₹120 · none if paid online' in the after-add card, not only in the drawer.

Ad-to-asset map (C17): the person who launches ads adopts the utm_content convention <piece>_<asset>_<angle> (e.g. prism_riya_reel1, prism_studio_colour) and keeps the token → frame/chip map current; they also say what prism_sugar_p1 shows.

Courier API (C1, C5): pincode-backed dates and per-pincode COD. serviceability.ts already keeps J&K/Ladakh, Bihar, Jharkhand, the North East and the islands prepaid-only. Confirm whether Fastrr enforces the same, because an unconditional 'COD available' on screen 1 would then be wrong for those shoppers; add the existing pincode check inside the delivery fold.
Owner confirms the ₹3,999 compare-at basis (C3), and decides whether store-level proof such as orders shipped may ever appear (currently barred by the strict reading of the Never list).
Optional policy upgrade (C5): a 7-day exchange on unworn pieces would let the trust row carry a real promise (Baymard: 60% look for the policy on the PDP, 15% abandoned over it) [S1].
Content (C10, C12, C13): a 6–10 s macro turn under 1 MB, more labelled creator clips, a dimension-marked wrist photo, and originals at least 1,440px wide.

TEST PLAN, infrastructure: client-side 50/50 split by naira_vid hash, persisted. Pass the arm to Fastrr through the existing sessionUtmParams (e.g. utm_term=pdp_a/pdp_b) so Shopify orders carry it; set it as a Clarity tag. Freeze the ladder for the whole test (it changed 4–5 times in 30 days and moved the 2+ share between 23% and 42%). Test the TEMPLATE across all jewellery PDPs: Prism alone sells about 10 units a month and can never reach significance.

TEST PLAN, test 1 (new PDP vs live JewelDetailNext, mobile only, about 8,000 mobile browser VC a week). Primary: InitiateCheckout per PDP visitor; base about 3%, and +20% relative needs about 13,900 visitors per arm, about 3.5 weeks. Secondary: ATC/VC; base about 13.5%, +15% needs about 4,750 per arm, about 1.2 weeks; expect +15–30% because the ladder, delivery, COD and the add button move onto screen 1. Also ATC→IC; expect 20% → 26–30% from Checkout-in-bar. Guardrails from Shopify orders by arm: AOV, items per order (expect 1.51 → 1.6+ from the vertical rail with 'adds ₹659'), prepaid share, cancellations, and RTO matured at 3 weeks. Orders/VC is directional only: +20% would need about 50,000 visitors per arm, about 12 weeks.

TEST PLAN, measurement hygiene before launch: Buy now must fire AddToCart then InitiateCheckout, otherwise ATC/VC falls artificially in the treatment arm. The 'Added' state must never fire a second AddToCart. Judge on browser-only pixel events plus Shopify orders, never on Shopify sessions (blind to the site) or Meta purchases (243 attributed against 206 orders).
TEST PLAN, test 2 after test 1 (needs the owner's prepaid decision): Buy now shows 'Pay online: ₹2,279' vs plain. Primary: prepaid share. Guardrail: IC/VC. Read the RTO outcome after 3 weeks.
RUM inside the Instagram webview (C16): field LCP and bytes before scroll, to replace lab-only scoring.
